;Armed conflicts and attacks
*A 32-year-old [[Syrians in Germany|Syrian]] man rams a stolen truck into eight cars in [[Limburg an der Lahn]], [[Hesse]], causing eight injuries. [[German police]] believe it was intentional, but the motive is yet to be determined. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/08/eight-hurt-as-stolen-truck-crashes-into-cars-in-germany (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Jalalabad suicide bombing]]
**A bomb on a [[rickshaw]] detonates as a [[minibus]] carrying new [[Afghan National Army|army]] recruits passes in [[Jalalabad]], [[Nangarhar Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. A military spokesperson says ten, including a child, were killed and a further 27 wounded. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/afghan-official-says-bomb-kills-at-least-10-in-eastern-city/2019/10/07/7d54ccb0-e904-11e9-a329-7378fbfa1b63_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (2015–present)]], [[International military intervention against ISIL]], [[Northern Syria Buffer Zone]]	
**U.S. forces begin to withdraw from [[Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria|northern Syria]]. [https://foreignpolicy.com/2019/10/07/erdogan-defying-pentagon-trump-endorses-turkish-operation-in-syria/ (Foreign Policy)]
**The [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] calls the U.S. withdrawal a "stab in the back". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-49956698 (BBC News)]
**A [[United States Department of Defense|U.S. Department of Defense]] spokesperson says [[Turkey]] has been pulled off the [[Combined Air Operations Centre]]'s [[air tasking order]] and that the U.S. has halted sharing [[aerial surveillance]] information with Turkey. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20191008-us-cuts-turkeys-access-to-north-east-syria-airspace-ahead-of-military-campaign/ (Middle East Monitor)] [https://www.militarytimes.com/flashpoints/2019/10/07/how-the-us-troop-withdrawal-from-northern-syria-could-create-an-isis-resurgence/ (Military Times)]
**[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Lindsey Graham]] strongly criticizes President Trump's decision, describing the event as "a big win for [[Iran]] and [[Bashar al-Assad|Assad]] [and] a big win for [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]". Former American envoy [[Brett McGurk]] mentions the 60,000 SDF-held ISIL detainees, saying that the [[United States Department of State|State Department]] and [[Office of Inspector General (United States)|inspectors general]] at the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] warn they are the "nucleus for a resurgent ISIL". [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/07/us-to-let-turkish-forces-move-into-syria-abandoning-kurdish-allies (''The Guardian'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[Censorship in China]]
**[[China]] bans American [[animated sitcom]] ''[[South Park]]'' in response to the episode "[[Band in China]]" which parodied censorship in China and Chinese influence on [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]]. [https://nypost.com/2019/10/07/south-park-banned-from-chinese-internet-after-band-in-china-episode/ (''New York Post'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/10/07/us/south-park-apology-chinese-internet-trnd/index.html (CNN)] [https://globalnews.ca/news/6001579/south-park-banned-in-china/ (Global News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic effects of Brexit]]
**Holger Bingmann, head of the [[Bundesverband Großhandel, Außenhandel, Dienstleistungen|Federation of German Wholesale, Foreign Trade and Services]], tells journalists [[Economy of Germany|German businesses]] have lost [[euro|€]]3.5 billion so far this year due to [[Brexit]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/german-businesses-already-incurring-brexit-losses-says-industry-boss/a-50725851 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[PizzaExpress|Pizza Express]], a [[United Kingdom|UK]]-based chain with 470 restaurants, including 150 overseas, reportedly hires [[financial advisor]]s ahead of talks with its [[creditor]]s. The business is [[pound sterling|£]]1.1 billion in debt and has made a loss for two consecutive years. It employs around 14,000 people. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-49957551 (BBC News)]
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**Citing [[Human rights in China|human rights]] issues, the [[United States Department of Commerce]] puts 20 Chinese [[Public security bureau (China)|public security bureaus]] and eight [[high tech]] companies, such as [[Hikvision|HikVision]], [[SenseTime]] and [[Megvii]], on the [[Export Administration Regulations]] entities [[blacklist]]. Like [[Huawei]], which was sanctioned on an identical blueprint for [[National security of the United States|national security]] reasons, the entities will need U.S. government approval before they can purchase components from U.S. companies. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-china-exclusive/u-s-expands-blacklist-to-include-chinas-top-ai-startups-ahead-of-trade-talks-idUSKBN1WM25M (Reuters)] [https://www.freightwaves.com/news/commerce-adds-28-chinese-firms-to-entity-list (American Shipper)]

;Disasters and accidents
*The [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Ministry of Transport (Ukraine)|Ministry of Transport]] announces it has revoked the [[air operator's certificate]] of [[Ukraine Air Alliance]], effective from October 5. The move results from the October 4 crash of an [[Antonov An-12]] owned by the airline, after it ran out of fuel near [[Lviv]], [[Ukraine]]. The decision was taken the same day. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4cd99477 (The Aviation Herald)]
*A [[North Korea]]n fishing boat collides with a [[Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)|Japanese Fisheries Agency]] vessel and sinks off [[Japan]]. At least 20 North Koreans are pulled from the water. The Japanese ship had been attempting to warn the North Korean vessel away from Japanese territory. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-07/20-north-korean-fishermen-overboard-after-collision-nhk-says (Bloomberg)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/10/06/world/asia/japan-north-korea-ship.html (''The New York Times'')]
*An overloaded ship carrying migrants capsizes and sinks off the island of [[Lampedusa]], [[Italy]], in rough conditions in the [[Mediterranean Sea]]. [[Search and rescue]] is underway; of at least 50 on board, 22 survivors have been saved and 13 bodies found. The deceased and missing both include pregnant women. The [[International Organization for Migration]] states the boat had departed from [[Tunisia]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/italy-death-toll-continues-to-rise-after-migrant-ship-sinks-in-mediterranean/a-50720302 (Deutsche Welle)]

;Law and crime
*King [[Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden]] decides that the children of [[Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland|Prince Carl Philip]] and [[Princess Sofia, Duchess of Värmland|Princess Sofia]], and the children of [[Princess Madeleine, Duchess of Hälsingland and Gästrikland|Princess Madeleine]] and [[Christopher O'Neill]] will no longer be members of the [[Swedish royal family#Royal House|Royal House of Sweden]]. The purpose of the decision is to establish which members of the Royal House may be expected to perform official duties incumbent on the Head of State or related to the function of the Head of State. [https://www.kungahuset.se/royalcourt/latestnews/latestnews/communiqueonchangestotheroyalhouse.5.18cc416116d61fe304a87a9.html (Swedish Royal Court)]
*In [[Lower Manhattan]], [[New York City]], a 24-year-old [[Homelessness in the United States|homeless]] man is charged with [[murder (United States law)|murdering]] four other homeless men and attempting to murder a fifth in random attacks. Authorities identify one of the deceased as an 83-year-old man, but release no further details about the victims. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/new-york-homeless-murder-beaten-death-sleep-manhattan-chinatown-randy-santos-a9145641.html (''The Independent'')]
*Two protestors who were arrested in [[Rostov-on-Don]] in 2017 while holding signs seeking resignations from the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]], and have been in custody since, are sentenced to over six years each in high-security prisons. They were charged with planning violent mass disturbances, and said that they confessed during torture. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/anti-putin-protesters-jailed-for-six-years-rbzttnhqv# (''The Times'')]
*The [[Supreme Court of the United States]] opens its 2019–2020 nine-month term with eight of its nine justices present. [[Ruth Bader Ginsburg|Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg]], who underwent a number of medical procedures for cancer throughout the past year, was present, but [[Clarence Thomas|Justice Clarence Thomas]] was absent "due to an unspecified illness." [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/us-supreme-court-kicks-off-new-term-with-justice-thomas-absent/ar-AAIp97d?ocid=spartandhp (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**The first people are charged with breaking the ban on wearing face masks in [[Hong Kong]]. The [[government of Hong Kong]] says the prohibition of face masks is needed to end months of violent protests. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/07/hong-kong-protests-charges-anti-face-mask-laws (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Tax returns of Donald Trump]]
**A judge rules against U.S. President [[Donald Trump]], ordering him to release eight years of state tax returns to New York officials. The defense makes an immediate appeal to the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit|Second Circuit Court of Appeals]], and is granted a temporary stay "pending expedited review." [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49963910 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*The [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] is awarded to [[Peter J. Ratcliffe]], [[William Kaelin Jr.]] and [[Gregg L. Semenza]] for their discoveries of how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/10/07/health/nobel-prize-medicine.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Astronomers announce the discovery of 20 new [[moons of Saturn|moons around Saturn]], adding to the 62 previously known. The new moons comprise 17 retrograde moons in the [[Saturn's Norse group of satellites|Norse group]] and three prograde moons, two of which belong to the [[Saturn's Inuit group of satellites|Inuit group]]. [https://phys.org/news/2019-10-saturn-surpasses-kupiter-discovery-moonsand.html (Phys.org)]
